summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted due to persistent steal syndrome symptoms in his left hand despite prior fistula banding. He reported chronic coldness and severe pain during dialysis, requiring early session termination. Hypotension was noted, prompting temporary hold of diltiazem and isosorbide. After cardiology consultation, he was restarted on a lower dose of diltiazem and initiated on digoxin and midodrine before dialysis, which improved blood pressure and reduced steal symptoms. An arteriogram showed no major arterial blockages but persistent poor distal radial and ulnar artery filling, even after fistula compression and nitroglycerin. A healing, non-displaced mid-humerus fracture was incidentally found on X-ray, contributing to shoulder pain. He responded well to treatment, completed dialysis without pain, and was discharged to an extended care facility with medication adjustments, fistula monitoring instructions, and plans for digoxin level checks.
